speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction, and have you noticed any other instances of prolonged bleeding or easy bruising in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience frequent nosebleeds or bleeding from your gums after brushing your teeth? Additionally, have you ever experienced pain or swelling in your joints without any known injury?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling, I need to rule out hemophilia, so I will request specific coagulation studies. REQUEST TEST: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT), Prothrombin Time (PT), and Factor VIII and IX levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the aPTT is prolonged but PT is normal, this points towards a deficiency in the intrinsic pathway, such as Hemophilia A or B. To distinguish between Factor VIII and Factor IX deficiency, I will request specific factor assays. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, this rules out Hemophilia A and B, suggesting a different coagulation factor deficiency like Factor XI or a platelet disorder. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI level and Platelet Function Assay

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal Factor XI and platelet function assays, the prolonged aPTT likely indicates a specific factor deficiency or inhibitor, so I will request tests for von Willebrand factor and Factor XIII. REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity, and Factor XIII Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity: Not available in current data, Factor XIII Activity: Not available in current data

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the vWF and Factor XIII results are unavailable, I need to look at the platelet count to rule out thrombocytopenia as a cause for the bleeding and bruising. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal platelets and an isolated prolonged aPTT that doesn't correct with standard factor assays, I suspect a coagulation inhibitor like lupus anticoagulant. REQUEST TEST: Mixing Study and Lupus Anticoagulant Assay

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal mixing study and lupus anticoagulant, the prolonged aPTT is likely due to a deficiency in Factor XII, which does not cause clinical bleeding. However, your symptoms suggest a platelet function issue missed by initial assays, so I need to see the vWF results. REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C (Factor XI Deficiency)
